Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:10:2.hebrew: לא אכל - דגזל נינהו, שהבעלים לא ידעו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:10:2.english: [He] did not eat - For they are stolen [property], since the owner did not know.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:11:1.hebrew: אם נמצאו יפות כו' - אלמא גלי דעתיה דניחא ליה, ה"נ גלי דעתיה דניחא ליה במה שנתן לנו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:11:1.english: If better [produce] is found, etc. - Thus, he revealed his intent that he is amenable [to it]; so too here, he revealed his intent that he is amenable to what [the sharecropper] gave us.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:11:2.english: They did not say "go to the better [fruits]" - that it is a revelation of intent, except with regard to the matter of terumah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:12:1.english: The dew is still upon them - [This refers to] one who brings his produce up to the roof and the dew descended upon them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:12:2.english: And he was glad - at the dew that fell upon them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:12:3.english: This is [in the category of] "when [water] is placed" - And they have been rendered susceptible to ritual impurity from now and forever.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:12:4.english: They had dried - before he found them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:12:5.hebrew: אע"פ ששמח - עכשיו בטל שירד עליהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:12:5.english: Even though he was glad - Now, about the dew that had fallen upon them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:1:1.hebrew: ירדן - וכן שאר נהרות, ותנא זה על יד הירדן היה יושב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:1:1.english: Jordan - And likewise [for] other rivers, and this Tanna was dwelling by the Jordan.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:2:1.hebrew: בלסטים מזוין - ובחזקה נטלה הימנו, ומעיקרא ידע ומייאש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:2:1.english: [Referring to] an armed bandit - And he took it from him by force, and from the outset [the owner] knew and despaired.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:1.english: A river swept away his beams - Of this [person], and another [person] found them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:2.hebrew: הרי אלו כו' - ה"ג: הרי אלו שלו מפני שנתיאשו הבעלים, דכל שטיפת נהר, כקורות עצים ואבנים, הבעלים ידעו בה מיד, דיש לה קול:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:2.english: These [items] etc. - This is the reading: "These belong to him because the owners despaired" — for [regarding] any sweeping away by a river, such as beams, wood, and stones, the owners know about it immediately, since it has a report [i.e., becomes widely known].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:3.hebrew: הא סתמא - הא אם היתה אבידה אחרת, שאין לנו לומר שידעו הבעלים, לא הויא של מוצאה. קשיא לרבא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:3.english: But [in] an unspecified [case] - That is, if it were another lost item, where we cannot say that the owners knew [of its loss], it would not belong to its finder. [This is] a difficulty for Rava.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:4.hebrew: כשיכול להציל - ודכוותה במציאה אחרת, דבר שיש בו סימן דיכול ליתן סימן וליטול, מודינא בה דחייב להחזיר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:3:4.english: Where he is capable of rescuing - And similarly regarding another lost item — an item that has an identifying mark, where he is able to provide an identifying mark and take [it] — I concede regarding it that he is obligated to return [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:4:1.hebrew: אפילו אין מרדפין נמי - דסמכי אהצלה דלמחר וליומא אוחרא, ולא מייאשי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:4:1.english: Even [if] they are not pursuing [them] as well - For they rely on rescuing [them] tomorrow or another day, and do not despair.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:4:2.hebrew: ע"י הדחק - ואם לא ימהר להציל, לא יצילו. הלכך, אין מרדפין — אפקורי אפקרינהו, דהא ידעו ולא הצילו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:4:2.english: With difficulty - And if [he] does not hasten to rescue [them], they will not rescue [them]. Therefore, [if] they do not pursue [them], they have certainly declared them ownerless, for behold, they knew [of the loss] and did not rescue [them].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:5:2.english: And he gathered - For the sake of the owner.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:5:3.english: And if he is concerned - [that is,] the owner, and he objects to what this [person] did.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:5:4.english: Because of robbery - That he separated his terumah without his permission.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:6:1.english: Go to [the] better ones - You should have gone to [the] better ones to give from them to the kohen.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:7:1.hebrew: לא הוה ידע - אלמא כיון דלכי ידע דניחא ליה, אמרינן מעיקרא נמי ניחא ליה. ולענין יאוש נמי, כיון דלכי ידע מייאש, מעיקרא נמי הוי יאוש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:7:1.english: He did not know - Evidently, since when he finds out he is pleased [with it], we say that from the outset as well he was pleased [with it]. And regarding despair as well, since when he finds out he despairs, from the outset as well it is [considered] despair.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:8:1.hebrew: אתם גם אתם - כן תרימו גם אתם, מהכא נפקא לן שלוחו של אדם כמותו לתרומה, שהשליח שתרם, תרומתו תרומה. וכיון דשליחות מהכא נפקא לן, על כרחך שלוחכם דומיא דאתם בעינן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:8:1.english: “You,” “also you” - [The verse states:] “Thus you also shall set apart” — from here we derive [that] a person’s agent is like himself with respect to teruma, [meaning] that an agent who separates teruma, his teruma is [valid] teruma. And since agency is derived from here, perforce we require [that] your agent be similar to “you.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 22a:8:2.english: So too, your agent with your knowledge - [Meaning] that the owners appointed him [as] an agent.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:10:1.hebrew: מר זוטרא לא אכל - וא"ת: ואמאי לא אכל? האמר רבא פרק הגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיט.): אריסא מדנפשיה קא זבן! ויש לומר: דהתם שהביא האריס מבית, דמסתמא ממה שהגיע לחלקו מביא; אבל הכא שהביא מן הפרדס, היה חושש מר זוטרא שמא בשעת חלוקה לא יאמר לבעל הפרדס "תטול כנגד מה שנתתי להם". ורב אשי לא היה חושש לזה, ולכך אכל קודם שבא מרי בר איסק, משום דאריס מדנפשיה קא יהיב; דאין לומר שהיה סומך שיתרצה מרי בר איסק כשידע, דהלכה כאביי, ואע"ג דהשתא ניחא ליה — מעיקרא לא הוה ניחא ליה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:10:1.english: Mar Zutra did not eat - And if you will say: Why did he not eat? Did not Rava say in the chapter HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 119a) [that] a sharecropper sells from his own [portion]? One can answer that there [it refers to a case] where the sharecropper brought [produce] from [his] house, for presumably he brings from what fell to his share; but here, where he brought [it] from the orchard, Mar Zutra was concerned lest at the time of division he would not say to the owner of the orchard, "Take [an amount] corresponding to what I gave them." And Rav Ashi was not concerned about this, and therefore he ate before Mari bar Isak arrived, because a sharecropper gives from his own [portion]; for one cannot say that he was relying [on the assumption] that Mari bar Isak would consent when he found out, since the halakha follows Abaye, [and thus] even though he is pleased now, originally he was not pleased.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:1:1.hebrew: מה שנתן נתן - אתיא כר', דאמר בפרק הגוזל [בתרא] (ב"ק דף קיד.): סתם גנב וגזלן הוי יאוש בעלים:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:1:1.english: "That which he gave, he gave" - [This] follows [the view of] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says in the chapter [entitled] HaGozel [Batra] (Bava Kamma 114a): [In the case of] an ordinary thief or robber, there is despair of the owners.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:3:1.hebrew: שטף נהר קוריו עציו ואבניו - ה"ג: "אם נתיאשו הבעלים הרי אלו שלו". וצ"ל דמיירי ביכול להציל בקל אם רודף בשעת שטיפה, דאי לאו הכי הוה כזוטו של ים שאבוד ממנו ומכל אדם, ועל זה לא היה אומר "הא סתם לא". אלא איירי ביכול להציל בקל בשעת שטיפה ואפילו אין בהן סימן, ולפי שיעכבן עקולי ופשורי ויקחם שם, ואפי' יקדמו אחרים ויקחו יחזירום לו, לפי שניכר שהוא בעליו לפי שרדף מיד. וס"ד דמיירי דאם לא רדף מיד בשעת שטיפה שלא יכול עוד כלל להציל — כדמוכח בסיפא — לפי שיקחום אחרים כשיעכבום עקולי ופשורי ולא יחזירו לפי שאין בהן סימן. וה"פ: "אם נתיאשו הבעלים", דהיינו שהיו שם בשעת שטיפה ולא רדפו — ואפילו אומרים שאין מתיאשים אין בכך כלום, דודאי הן מתיאשים בלבן — "הא סתמא", שלא היו בעלים בשעת שטיפה ולא נתיאשו עד שידעו הבעלים ששטפה נהר, ואז כבר אינו יכול להציל לפי שאין בו סימן, "לא", דכשמצאן באיסורא אתא לידיה שהבעלים לא ידעו עדיין; אלמא יאוש שלא מדעת לא הוי יאוש. ומשני: ביכול להציל אפי' אחר שטיפה, כגון שיש באבידה סימן, שהבעלים אינן מתיאשין כשידעו. ופריך: "אי הכי אימא סיפא: ואם היו הבעלים מרדפין כו', מאי אריא מרדפין? אפילו היו בעלים שם בשעת שטיפה ולא רדפו נמי יחזיר!" ומשני: ביכול להציל אחר שטיפה ע"י הדחק, דאע"פ שיש בו סימן בטורח יכול להציל, לפי שיתרחקו הרבה שהנהר מוליכן ברחוק; ולכך אם היה בשעת שטיפה ואינו מרדף ודאי מתיאש, כיון שעתה יכול להציל בלא דוחק ואינו מציל, אבל אין הבעלים בשעת שטיפה יחזיר, דכשידעו הבעלים לא יתיאשו ויצילו על ידי הדחק. וא"ת: מנלן הא סתמא חייב להחזיר? דלמא "נתיאשו" אתא לאפוקי שהיו שם ורדפו, דחייב להחזיר! וי"ל: דא"כ, לא ליתני "אם נתיאשו", אלא לתני סתמא "שטף נהר קוריו עציו ואבניו הרי אלו שלו", דפשיטא דלא מיירי ברדפו בשעת שטיפה, דהא קתני סיפא דאם היו הבעלים מרדפים חייב. ואין להקשות דמצי דייק מסיפא: טעמא דמרדפין, הא סתמא הרי אלו שלו — דלעולם נימא דהוא הדין סתמא דיחזיר, ולא נקט "מרדפין" אלא לאפוקי שהיו הבעלים בשעת שטיפה ולא רדפו; וע"י סיפא ידעינן דמיירי באין יכול להציל. אבל רש"י דגרס "מפני שנתיאשו הבעלים", משמע לישנא דפשיט ליה דנתיאשו; א"כ מרישא גופיה מצי לאוכוחי דמיירי באין יכול להציל ולא היה צריך להביא סיפא, ותו מנלן דהא סתמא לא, דאפילו סתמא נמי מצי מיירי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:3:1.english: If a river swept away his beams, his wood, or his stones - This is how we read [the baraita]: "If the owners despaired, these belong to him." And one must say that it is speaking of [a case] where he is able to rescue [them] easily if he pursues [them] at the time of the sweeping away, for if not so, it would be like the depths of the sea, where it is lost to him and to every person, and regarding that [the Gemara] would not say, "but in an unspecified case, no." Rather, it is speaking of [a case] where he is able to rescue [them] easily at the time of the sweeping away, even if there is no identifying mark on them, because bends and pools [of the river] will detain them and he can take them there; and even if others get there first and take [them], they will return [them] to him, because it is recognizable that he is their owner since he pursued [them] immediately. And [the Gemara] initially assumed that it is speaking of [a case] where if he did not pursue [them] immediately at the time of the sweeping away, he would no longer be able to rescue [them] at all — as is proven in the latter clause — because others would take them when the bends and pools detain them, and they would not return [them] since there is no identifying mark on them. And this is the explanation [of the Gemara's inference]: "If the owners despaired" — that is, they were there at the time of the sweeping away and did not pursue [them], and even if they say that they do not despair, that is of no consequence, for they certainly despair in their hearts — "but in an unspecified case," where the owners were not [there] at the time of the sweeping away, and they did not despair until the owners found out that the river swept [them] away, and by then he is already unable to rescue [them] since there is no identifying mark on them, "[they do] not [belong to the finder]," because when he found them, it came into his possession in a forbidden manner since the owners did not yet know; thus, unconscious despair is not [valid] despair. And [the Gemara] answers: [It is speaking of a case] where he is able to rescue [them] even after the sweeping away, such as where there is an identifying mark on the lost item, so that the owners do not despair when they find out. And [the Gemara] objects: "If so, say the latter clause: 'And if the owners were pursuing, etc.' Why specifically 'pursuing'? Even if the owners were there at the time of the sweeping away and did not pursue, he should also return [them]!" And [the Gemara] answers: [It is speaking of a case] where he is able to rescue [them] after the sweeping away with difficulty, for even though there is an identifying mark on it, he can [only] rescue [it] with exertion, because [the items] will have moved far away as the river carries them a great distance; therefore, if he was [there] at the time of the sweeping away and does not pursue, he certainly despairs, since now he can rescue [them] without difficulty and he does not rescue [them]; however, if the owners were not [there] at the time of the sweeping away, he must return [them], for when the owners find out they will not despair and will rescue [them] with difficulty. And if you ask: From where do we [know] that in an unspecified case he is obligated to return [them]? Perhaps "they despaired" comes to exclude [a case] where they were there and pursued, where he is obligated to return [them]! And one can answer: For if so, let [the baraita] not teach "if they despaired," rather let it teach without qualification: "If a river swept away his beams, his wood, or his stones, these belong to him," for it is obvious that it is not speaking of [a case] where they pursued at the time of the sweeping away, since the latter clause teaches that if the owners were pursuing, he is obligated [to return them]. And one should not object that one could infer from the latter clause: "The reason is that they are pursuing; but in an unspecified case, these belong to him" — for we can always say that the same applies to an unspecified case, that he must return [them], and it only stated "pursuing" to exclude [a case] where the owners were [there] at the time of the sweeping away and did not pursue; and through the latter clause we know that it is speaking of [a case] where he cannot rescue [them]. However, [according to] Rashi, who reads "because the owners despaired," the wording implies that it is obvious to him that they despaired; if so, from the first clause itself [the Gemara] could have proven that it is speaking of [a case] where he cannot rescue [them], and it would not have needed to bring the latter clause; and furthermore, from where do we [know] that "but in an unspecified case, no," for even an unspecified case could also be speaking [of where they despaired].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:6:1.hebrew: אם יש יפות מהן תרומתו תרומה - דמסתמא גם מתחילה היה דעתו כן. וא"ת: ונימא דהשתא ודאי ניחא ליה ביפות, אבל מתחילה בשעה שתרם אי הוה ידע לא הוה ניחא ליה, דאין דרך לתרום מן היפות — כדאמרינן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף כא:) גבי דבר שיש בו סימן, דאפילו לרבא חייב להכריז, דאע"ג דהשתא מתיאש אין בכך כלום? וי"ל, דשאני הכא, דכיון דחזינן ביה דניחא ליה השתא, אמרינן נמי ניחא ליה מעיקרא משום מצוה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:6:1.english: If there is better [produce] than it, his terumah is terumah - For presumably, from the outset as well, this was his intention. And if you ask: Let us say that now he is certainly pleased with the better [produce], but initially, at the time he separated terumah, had he known, he would not have been pleased, since it is not the practice to separate terumah from the better [produce] — just as we say above (Bava Metzia 21b) regarding an item that has an identifying mark, that even according to Rava, [the finder] is obligated to proclaim [it], for even though now [when he discovers the loss] he despairs [of recovering it], that is of no consequence? One can answer that it is different here, for since we see in him that he is pleased now, we also say that he was pleased from the outset on account of [it being] a mitzvah.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:8:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "<abbr title="הכי נמי">ה"נ</abbr> מסתברא דאי לא שוייה שליח", ולא גרסינן "ותסברא":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:8:1.english: This is the [correct] reading: "So too, it is reasonable, for if he did not designate him [as] an agent," and we do not read "And is it reasonable?"

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:9:1.hebrew: ואם לאו אין תרומתו תרומה - וא"ת, דבפרק אלמנה ניזונית (כתובות דף צט: ושם ד"ה פיחת) אמרינן דסתמיה דבעל הבית הוי אחד מחמשים, ואם השליח פיחת י' או הוסיף י' — תרומתו תרומה, דמצי א"ל: "בהכי אמדתיך", ה"נ נימא הכי? וי"ל, דהתם הוי כולה שיעור תרומה, ויש שתורם כך ויש שתורם כך, לכך מצי א"ל: "כיון שלא פירשת לי — בהכי אמדתיך"; אבל מיפות אין רגילות לתרום, ולכך לא היה לו לתרום בשום ענין מהם בלא רשותו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22a:9:1.english: But if not, his teruma is not teruma - And if you will ask: In the chapter [entitled] Almana Nizonet (Ketubot 99b, and there s.v. Piḥat), we say that the unspecified [intent] of a homeowner is one-fiftieth, and if the agent decreased [it by] ten or increased [it by] ten, his teruma is teruma, because he can say to him, "I assessed you to be [minded] thus" — here too, let us say so! And one can answer that there, all of it is [within the normal] measure of teruma, and there are those who separate teruma this way and there are those who separate teruma that way; therefore he can say to him, "Since you did not specify to me, I assessed you to be [minded] thus." However, from superior-quality [produce] it is not customary to separate teruma, and therefore he should not have separated teruma from them in any manner without his permission:
